subject.title: [Feature]: Scope Codex native hook relay spawns with per-tool hook matchers

question: Should per-tool matcher scope become the permanent plugin API contract across typed tool hooks, trusted-tool policies, and Codex tool-result middleware?
rationale: This choice adds compatibility-sensitive plugin API surface and determines security-critical behavior when tool names, aliases, matcher sets, or Codex versions differ.

options.title: Adopt one matcher contract
options.body: Approve one optional exact-name matcher type across all three surfaces, with omitted-as-match-all behavior and fail-closed fallback for uncertain Codex mappings.

options.title: Keep scope internal
options.body: Avoid public matcher fields and optimize relay spawning through an internal prepared-policy capability map or resident bridge.

options.title: Defer API expansion
options.body: Land process-level availability mitigations first and revisit tool-scoped plugin APIs after the broader relay architecture settles.

recommendation.title: Adopt one matcher contract
recommendation.body: Approve one optional exact-name matcher type across all three surfaces, with omitted-as-match-all behavior and fail-closed fallback for uncertain Codex mappings.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant merged history owns the current fail-closed fallback contract that matcher scoping must preserve.
